_comment: Work Lamar puts your way. Edited here, reloaded on script start.
ORDER MATTERS. He works down this list in the order it is written and offers you the
first one you have not finished. Only once every job here is behind you does he stop
deciding and let you pick. Finished jobs are remembered by id in the save, so adding a
job or moving one does not re-lock work you have already done.
id          stable key; never change it once a save references it
kind        BikeRide | RideOut | Hit | DriveBy
BikeRide  the scripted push-bike job -- fixed route, no guns on either side
RideOut   ride out, hands only, both sides
Hit       same trip, everybody armed, the corner shoots back
DriveBy   take a car past and shoot it up without stopping
name        the choice he offers you, in his words
brief       what he says when he explains it
done        what he says when you come back paid
targetGang  whose people you are going after -- their models and colours are used
zone        GET_NAME_OF_ZONE code the job happens in, used for the objective wording
x, y, z     the exact corner they stand on. Leave all three at 0 and the job falls back
to the middle of the zone, which for a big zone can be a block away from the
place you actually meant. BikeRide ignores these -- its route is fixed.
targets     how many of them are waiting
homies      how many of yours ride out with you
escapeHeat  true if the law turns up once the work is done. Lamar will not take it off
you until the stars are gone, so the trip home is part of the job.
heatStars   how many stars escapeHeat applies. Ignored when escapeHeat is false.
payMin/payMax  cash, rolled between the two
rep         standing with your own gang for finishing it
minRank     rank before he will offer it at all

missions.name: Get on a bike with me.
missions.brief: Aye. Frank. Come here, come here. Ballas been posted on the Chamberlain courts all week, sittin' on OUR rims like somebody handed 'em the keys to the gate. Ain't nobody hooped down there since Tuesday. TUESDAY, dawg. Little homies out playin' in the street behind this.
missions.done: HAAA! Look at my boy! Nah, look at US. That's how we used to get down at fifteen, and the whole court seen it, that's the part that count. Left, LEFT, told you that one. My hand hurt too, that's a real hand hurt. They ain't comin' back to that rim. And whatever else we got into on the way home -- that's between me, you and the bikes. Give me one second. One. MY plan.
missions.briefAgain: Aye. Same as before -- they back on the courts. I KNOW. Don't say nothin'. Grab a bike, it's hands, and don't be bringin' no strap out there this time neither.
missions.doneAgain: There it is. Same as last time, only quicker. Them boys gon' get real tired of learnin' this. And every time it happen, it's my name they hear before they hear yours.
briefMore: Now I could send somebody down there to get busy. I could. Straight up. But then it's laws all over this block by dinner over a damn basketball court, and everybody out here eatin' it for nothin'. Not over no hoop. We ain't spendin' a body on a rim. That's the difference between me and them fools.

So it's me and you. Just us, don't need nobody else for this -- two of us rollin' up on bikes says more than ten of us in cars anyway, that's psychology, dawg. Grab a bike and it's HANDS. Thought of that in the shower this mornin'. No straps, don't even have one on you. You pull somethin' out there and I ain't never met you. Who is that? Don't know him.
And after? We ride back, we sit down, and I'm tellin' you about this grow I been settin' up. I got ideas, cuz. I always got ideas.

missions.name: Spin Rancho, burn the whip.
missions.brief: Man, listen. Rancho is yellow top to bottom, and them fools ain't just standin' out there no more, Frank, they SERVIN'. In Chamberlain. On Davis. Corners we been holdin' since before your little ass could reach the pedals, and every dollar of it comin' out my pocket.
missions.done: Seen that smoke from here, cuz! No plate to run, no body to catch, and them Vagos out there arguin' about who did it 'cause don't none of 'em know. That's exactly how I called it, word for word. Me. LD. And Gerald ain't gotta hear about none of it.
missions.briefAgain: Vagos crept back on them corners. Yeah. Told you it wasn't a one time thing, that's why I keep sayin' it. Beater out front, spin through, then the whip goes same as before.
missions.doneAgain: Smoke again. Good. They gon' start thinkin' this block got somethin' wrong with it, and that's exactly what I want 'em thinkin'. That's a LD long game right there.
briefMore: And I can't touch they price 'cause they gettin' it straight off Madrazo people. So I take it to Gerald. Man look me dead in my eye and say leave it alone. So we goin' round Gerald. This me and you. And you spray those fools out there, hear me? Set been in pieces since Grove went purple. This a message, not no war.

Take that beater out front, spin through Jamestown, make some noise, and soon as one of 'em look up you gone. Then the whip go. That baseball pitch back of the Chamberlain flats, gas all over it, put one in it, walk off. Laws run plates, homie. They can't run your face.

missions.name: Cross this fool out.
missions.brief: Aye, you seen this busta UNIT? Big red letters, Forum Drive all the way down to the wash. And he named hisself UNIT. Like a storage unit. Like somethin' you rent, dawg. Fool run with Ballas people and he treatin' our whole side like it's his little sketchbook.
missions.done: Rolled past the one by the wash this mornin'. Boy, you MESSED that fool up. Ain't one letter of his left you can read -- just green all over the top of it like somebody was sick on his whole career. He gon' pull up on that and feel somethin' drop in his chest and he ain't even gon' be able to tell nobody why. Crossed out is crossed out. On my momma.
missions.briefAgain: That busta been out again. New letters, same weak hand. You know where they at and you know what a can is for -- go do it.
missions.doneAgain: Covered again. He gon' keep comin' back and we gon' keep goin' over him and one day he gon' work out that's just how it is out here. Slow learner. Some people is.
briefMore: And where WE at? Nowhere. His letters all up our side and can't nobody be bothered to go over 'em, and I gotta drive past 'em every mornin'. That's how a block quit bein' yours, Frank. Ain't a shot get fired. Some little homie just grow up here seein' who got the walls, and go bang with somebody else.

So get a bike, get a can, and go straight over the top of him. Four of his, all local. And go by yourself. Two dudes on bikes with cans is a whole story for the laws, one dude is just a kid on a bike. That's psychology right there. LD psychology.

missions.name: The cut house in Rancho.
missions.brief: Aight. Messages ain't movin' 'em, still out there, still servin', so we done sendin' letters. Vagos got a lil cut house out Rancho where they break the weight down before it ever touch our side. Five of 'em in there, comfortable, actin' like it's somebody auntie barbecue.
missions.done: I heard about that before you was even off the freeway, dawg. Phone been ringin' all mornin' and every last one of 'em sayin' LD sent him. LD SENT HIM. Five of them people gotta go buy that weight twice now, and my name is what did it to 'em. TAKE that.
missions.briefAgain: They opened that cut house back up. Different house, same fools, same weight. Take three and go do it properly again -- you know how it goes now, I ain't walkin' you through it.
missions.doneAgain: Phone ringin' again this mornin'. Every time we take that off 'em they gotta go buy it twice, and every time it get more expensive to be them. That's the whole plan workin'.
briefMore: And don't be standin' there thinkin' on it, I already did the thinkin' for the both of us, that's what I'm here for. You take that off 'em they gotta go buy more, and buyin' more cost 'em. Cost 'em enough times and all of a sudden our price look real reasonable again.

Three homies, everybody with a machine pistol. Don't bring no shotgun in there, this ain't duck season, you want somethin' that spray. And somebody in that house ALWAYS call the laws, so shake 'em way off you before you come back round my block.

One more thing and this the important one. Them three is yours till it's done. You go through that door, they comin' through it behind you, and can't nobody in there talk 'em out of it. Only thing they won't do is think for you. That part's still on you, cuz.

And look at what you rollin' in before you go. If it's that German whip out front, that ain't no ditch car, dawg, that's a payday with doors on it. Shake the laws first, THEN run it down to Hao -- he change the numbers, we both eat. Anything else, leave it wherever you like. Either way you walkin' back to me for the money.

missions.name: Get 'em off Grove.
missions.brief: Ballas standin' on Grove. On GROVE, Frank. My granddaddy raised nine kids on that street. We buried that man out the church on the corner. And now I gotta hear about a whole line of purple leanin' on the same fence he painted with his own hands. Nah, dawg. Nah.
missions.done: THAT'S what I'm talkin' about! Didn't even slow down, cuz, just come through and it was done. Old heads on the porch tellin' it to each other like they was out there watchin', and can't none of 'em say who was in the car. Granddaddy woulda shook my hand behind this one. Yours too. But mine first.
missions.briefAgain: Purple on Grove again. I ain't even mad no more, I'm just tired. Take three, keep it rollin', don't stop on that street. Go.
missions.doneAgain: Off it again. Old heads seen it again too. Granddaddy ain't gotta hear about it twice, but he'd have liked knowin' it stayed ours. That's on both of us. Mostly me.
briefMore: And yeah, I know it's theirs on paper, everybody know that. But it's theirs on paper, and then it's them STANDIN' on it grinnin', and once the old heads quit callin' it ours it's gone for real. Then it ain't a set no more. It's just a street with a sign on it.

You don't stop on Grove. That's the whole thing. Take three homies, EVERYBODY carry, and you keep that car ROLLIN' -- past the fence, down the block, gone. Hands was for the courts, this ain't the courts, and a man standin' still on that street is a man on somebody porch camera. You gon' catch the laws comin' off it too, that's a promise, not a maybe. Don't you dare drag 'em back round here to me.
And you know the rest. German whip out front, that one don't get left nowhere -- laws first, then Hao. I ain't sayin' it twice.

missions.name: We goin' huntin'.
missions.brief: Ay. Ay, Frank. Sit down. Nah -- stand UP, this a standin'-up conversation. Somebody been creepin' up on the Hills at night. Three weeks now. No shots, no horns, no nothin' -- they come, they take somethin', and they gone 'fore anybody even know they was on the block.
missions.done: Ay! AY! You SEEN that?! Man never even turned ROUND! Frank, we was out there like them dudes off the nature channel -- belly in the grass, wind in they face, creepin' on a antelope for four hours straight. And the whole time I got that British nigga whisperin' in my head. "The predator waits." THE PREDATOR WAITS, Frank. We was the documentary. And them fools was the antelope and didn't even KNOW they was the antelope. Three weeks they been creepin' up on us -- tonight we out-crept 'em. On my mama. Now give me my knife back.
missions.briefAgain: Same as before, cuz. Four Ballers, Davis and Rancho, just use the knife. Get up behind 'em and do it quiet.
missions.doneAgain: Four corners, quiet feet, straight back out they neighbourhood. Antelope again, dawg. I keep tellin' people how we be movin' out there and don't nobody believe me.
briefMore: And this where I stop playin' with you. They put the little homie in the hospital with a bat and had him tellin' me he fell down some stairs. Stairs, Frank. Boy live in a bungalow. Took another one phone, took his money, sent him home talkin' about some stranger did it. Quiet. Every time. Three weeks, and don't nobody say a word to me.

Well now we got 'em. Four Ballas -- and they ain't even hidin', dawg, they right back on they own corners in Davis and Rancho like wasn't nothin' happened. Standin' out there all day. So I'm in the pawn shop buyin' a TV, I look in the case, and there it is. Big ass Rambo knife. Serrated down the back, compass in the handle, li'l matches in there TOO, case you get lost. Walked out with no TV. They came to us quiet -- we goin' to them the exact same way.

Now that's THEY neighbourhood, Frank, so can't nothin' go loud out there. I'ma tell you which one we on. They be standin' round on they phone all day like they got a career -- you come up on his BACK, you stick him, and he never even knew nobody was on the street with him. They leave marks where they walked, so follow 'em. One of 'em turn round and clock you, he ain't runnin' nowhere, he comin', and that one don't count for us no more. Three out the four and we good. Grove Street last, 'cause Grove the deepest in and it's full of they people -- second he drop, we gone.

missions.name: Spin they route in La Mesa.
missions.brief: La Mesa. Vagos been runnin' packs through there all month. Same weight, half the price, and every gram of it comin' straight out our corners' pocket. Our little homies standin' out all night for damn near nothin' 'cause some fool three blocks over sellin' cheaper.
missions.done: Ha! Watch. Them people gon' be checkin' they mirrors at every light for a month, drivin' all the way around to get somewhere three blocks off they own street. And it's my name doin' that to 'em. Six for six, my boy. And I made you.
missions.briefAgain: They runnin' that route again 'cause they think we forgot. Same as before -- through, loud, gone. Don't be sittin' out there.
missions.doneAgain: HA. Twice. Now it ain't a warnin' no more, now it's a pattern, and a pattern is what make a man change his whole route. That's chess again, homie. Still don't play.
briefMore: We took the Rancho spot and they just opened another one, right? That's what happen when a man got more spots than you got bodies. So forget spots. We make the ROUTE cost 'em instead. Can't nobody keep drivin' a street they been shot at on. That's chess, homie. And I don't even play.

Roll through, make it LOUD, be gone before the laws finish they donut. Don't be sittin' out there tryna prove somethin' to nobody, that's how you end up in somebody photograph. In and out, my boy. It's a message, not a visit.
And look what's out front before you pull off. You know what it is and you know where it goes. Don't make me the man who explains the same thing every time he see you.

missions.name: Anything, Franklin.
missions.brief: Franklin. Come here. Close the -- nah, leave it, it's a shop. Aight, check it. You know how I been sayin' the basement is square footage? Square footage need STOCK, homie. And I been buyin' off a little dude in Davis four months at a number I ain't sayin' out loud in my own store.
briefMore: So. Six weeks back a man walk in here and buy every fluorescent I got. Every one. Tubes, ballasts, them long cords -- four hundred bucks of lightin', cash in my hand, straight out the door. Tells me it's for a car showroom. Now I'm standin' there thinkin', that is a LOT of light for a car showroom. And he lookin' at me thinkin', this dude got a basement. And we just kinda nodded at each other, Franklin. That's business. That's how it happen.

So we been talkin' since. On the phone. The SHOP phone -- I ain't givin' a man I never met my personal, I ain't stupid. His name Ardo. Or Arto. It's one of them, the line ain't great down here, it's all that metal. And Ardo say he can do me a whole key for twenty-two five. TWENTY-TWO FIVE, Franklin. That's half what it's worth and he said it like he readin' me a menu. Today. Rogers Scrap, out by the freeway.

And before you say it -- yeah. I know what them dudes is known for. And I asked him about it straight up, 'cause I'm a professional. And he said, and I'm quotin' him word for word: we can get anything. ANYTHING, Franklin. That's a man who understands demand. Pops would've loved him.

And I'm comin' with you. Don't pull that face -- it's my money, it's my guy, and I ain't never met the man neither so somebody gotta do the introductions. You just drive and stand there lookin' like that, I already told him you my head of security. Oh -- and I give him eight up front to hold it, so don't be negotiatin'. That part's gone either way.
missions.briefAgain: Same as before. Rogers Scrap, twenty-two five less the eight I already give him, a man called Ardo. Or Arto. And I'm ridin' with you again, so don't be pullin' off while I'm still openin' the door.
missions.done: ...they was ALWAYS gon' do that. Wasn't they. There was three of 'em on that yard before we even -- one of 'em was on the ROOF, Franklin. Who gets on a ROOF for a conversation? -- nah. Nah, I'm not mad, I'm processin'. And I gave that man TRADE price on them tubes. Trade price, Frank. That's what's hurtin' me. ... Is that it? That's more than a key. That's a lot more than a key. Put it down. Don't hold it like that, put it DOWN. Aight. Aight. So we up.
missions.doneAgain: Same man, same two o'clock, same outcome. I'm startin' to think Ardo was never gon' hand me nothin'. Bring it downstairs. And Franklin -- new phone. I threw the shop one in the canal.
